macro: US equity futures are in the red Thursday morning with the S&P down 44 points, Nasdaq off 105 basis points, and European indices sliding 50-60 basis points led by weakness in industrials, autos, tech, and banks. Asian markets were mostly lower overnight with China's Shanghai Composite falling 1.22% and Shenzhen dropping nearly 2%. The key macro driver is Brent crude spiking 275 basis points back to roughly $106 as US-Iran diplomatic talks show little real progress, compounding the yield pressure already set in motion by Wednesday's blowout flash PMIs.
rates_fed: Two-year Treasury yields are flat while 10 and 30-year yields climb 2-3 basis points, extending gains from Wednesday's hot PMI data. The market is now pricing in 38 basis points of incremental Fed hikes this year with odds of an October 28th increase above 70%, plus an additional roughly 55 basis points in 2027. Fed Governor Barr on Wednesday became the latest official to signal further tightening is needed, and the Japanese yen continues to weaken, creeping back toward 160 versus the dollar.
market_outlook: Adam is bearish-leaning heading into Thursday's session. The dual headwinds of rising oil prices and climbing long-end yields — both driven by geopolitical stalemate on Iran — are the primary pressure points, and the Trump-Xi summit is expected to disappoint with only a modest two-month extension of the Busan trade agreement. The key catalyst to watch is the Trump-Xi meeting at the White House starting around 10am Eastern, alongside any developments on the Iran diplomatic front.
bull_case: The yield problem is now severe enough that it should refocus the White House and Treasury on policies to bring rates lower, with Iran policy being the most immediate lever the administration controls. Any surprise breakthrough on US-Iran talks could send oil sharply lower and provide meaningful relief to both yields and equities. The Trump-Xi summit, even if underwhelming, at least extends the current trade truce and avoids an escalation scenario. DRI earnings before the open and COST after the close could provide positive micro catalysts if they beat expectations.
bear_case: Brent crude is back at $106 after briefly dipping below $100, and there is no clear catalyst to reverse the trend given Iran's strengthened negotiating position and its proxies' growing regional influence. Long-end yields are grinding higher on the back of hot PMIs and sticky energy-driven inflation, creating a toxic mix for equity multiples. The Trump-Xi summit is shaping up to be a non-event with no new Boeing orders and only a two-month trade truce extension, removing a potential positive catalyst. The aggregate news flow from the AI industry has been net negative over the past week, weighing on high-multiple tech names.

company_items.summary: Zuckerberg's Meta Connect keynote Wednesday night was viewed as at best inline with expectations. While AI narrative around Muse's momentum remains positive, the broader AI industry news flow over the past week has been net negative in aggregate, limiting the upside from the event.

Boeing will likely not receive any incremental plane orders from China during the Trump-Xi summit, with the company instead focused on finalizing the 200-unit order announced back in May. This removes a key positive catalyst that markets had been anticipating from the high-profile diplomatic meeting.

Google is nearing the release of its next-generation flagship frontier model, Gemini 4, according to the head of its DeepMind unit. This positions Google competitively in the accelerating frontier model race, though the broader AI news flow backdrop remains net negative for the sector.

An FDA advisory committee recommended approval for Grail's multicancer early detection blood test, though support was described as somewhat tepid regarding effectiveness and overall benefits. The outcome was largely expected following the earlier publication of briefing documents, limiting incremental upside surprise.

Starboard Value is pushing Knife River to explore a sale, adding activist pressure to the construction materials company. This is a classic activist-driven strategic review catalyst that typically provides a floor under the stock price.

McDonald's shares slumped after the company warned at its analyst meeting that Q3 comparable sales are tracking slightly below consensus and that free cash flow conversion will come in below prior guidance due to higher capital spending. The company did offer a 2030 operating margin target ahead of expectations, but near-term disappointment dominated the reaction.

Barry Diller on Wednesday withdrew People Inc's proposed takeout bid for MGM Resorts but stated he remains open to and interested in a strategic transaction with the casino giant. The withdrawal removes a hard bid catalyst, though Diller's continued interest keeps some takeover premium in the stock.

Paramount is looking to raise equity as the Warner deal moves closer to completion and is reportedly considering approaching Elon Musk for an investment to bolster its balance sheet. Equity issuance is typically dilutive, though the strategic rationale around the Warner deal could provide longer-term upside.

HB Fuller reported modest upside on EPS of $1.52 versus the Street's $1.46, driven by margin expansion with gross margins up 120 basis points and EBITDA margins up 80 basis points as pricing increases offset raw material inflation. Sales were inline at $938 million and full-year guidance was left roughly unchanged with the EPS midpoint moving slightly to $4.77 from $4.75.

Eli Lilly struck a research collaboration and licensing agreement with China's InnoCare Pharma worth up to $3.35 billion. The deal expands Lilly's pipeline exposure and reflects continued aggressive investment in broadening its therapeutic reach beyond its blockbuster GLP-1 franchise.

sectors: Energy is the key sector to watch — Brent back at $106 is a tailwind for energy stocks but a headwind for the broad market via yields and inflation. Tech and AI-linked names face headwind from net negative industry news flow over the past week, AI discounting trends reported by The Information, and a Meta keynote that failed to exceed expectations. Industrials are underperforming in Europe. Consumer discretionary faces pressure from McDonald's guidance cut. Healthcare gets a modest positive from Grail's FDA advisory committee recommendation. Nicotine and tobacco names could see upside if the FDA moves to ease restrictions on vape and pouch product authorizations.

tts_summary:
Good morning. Here is your morning game plan for Thursday September 24th.

The macro picture is deteriorating on two fronts simultaneously — energy and rates. Brent crude has spiked 275 basis points this morning back to roughly $106 a barrel, erasing the brief dip below $100 we saw just 36 hours ago. The catalyst is simple: there is no meaningful progress on the US-Iran diplomatic front. Whatever optimism Trump's Tuesday comments generated has been walked back by subsequent reporting, and with Iranian proxies controlling the Bab al-Mandab Strait and targeting Saudi infrastructure, Iran has little incentive to make concessions. Meanwhile, ten and thirty-year Treasury yields are climbing another 2 to 3 basis points this morning, extending Wednesday's surge that was triggered by blowout flash PMI data. The market is now pricing over 70% odds of a Fed hike on October 28th, with another roughly 55 basis points expected next year. Futures reflect the pressure — the S&P is off 44 points, the Nasdaq is down over 100 basis points, and European indices are sliding 50 to 60 basis points.

On the company side, the big story is what is not happening. Boeing is not getting any incremental plane orders from China at the Trump-Xi summit. That removes a baseline positive catalyst from one of the marquee geopolitical events of the week. The summit itself is shaping up as largely ceremonial — the headline outcome is a two-month extension of the Busan trade agreement, pushing the deadline from November 10th to January 10th. That is underwhelming. Adam's base case is status quo, not breakthrough.

Meta's Connect keynote from Zuckerberg Wednesday night landed as roughly inline with expectations at best. The AI narrative around Muse has momentum, but aggregate AI industry news flow over the past week has been net negative — enterprises are pushing back on full-price AI tools, discounting is accelerating, and open-source models are compressing margins across the space. Google is a relative bright spot, with the head of DeepMind signaling that Gemini 4, its next flagship frontier model, is close to release.

McDonald's is under pressure after warning at its analyst day that third quarter comparable sales are tracking slightly below consensus and that free cash flow conversion will disappoint due to higher capex. Grail got an FDA advisory committee recommendation for its multicancer blood test, though the support was tepid and the outcome was widely anticipated. Eli Lilly announced a partnership with China's InnoCare worth up to $3.35 billion, a positive pipeline extension. Knife River has Starboard Value pushing for a sale, which provides a floor. And Barry Diller withdrew his formal MGM bid but left the door open for a future deal, making that stock a mixed read.

Directionally, Adam is leaning bearish into today's session. The yield and oil combination is the dominant headwind, and without a positive surprise from the Trump-Xi meeting or an Iran headline, there is no obvious catalyst to reverse the pressure. The one structural bull argument is that rates are now painful enough that they should force the White House to act — and the most immediate lever they control is Iran policy. Watch the summit around 10am Eastern and watch the Iran headlines all day. Those are your two binary risk events. DRI reports before the open and Costco reports after the close, so there are micro catalysts on both ends. Stay sharp.
